correctness.rationale: For each finite section the comb embeds isometrically as leaves of a weighted real tree. Exactly three classes of edges give formula (1) with all endpoints included; independent one-Lipschitz edge slopes show both upper and lower norm bounds. The finite free-space unit ball is the closed absolutely convex hull of normalized two-point molecules, permitting exact operator-norm reduction. Sign changes in a contiguous molecule add precisely a_i per flip and binary coordinate runs contribute precisely their starting heights. Strict decrease proves the alternating-singleton maximizer. Taking compatible finite-section suprema is valid without assuming unconditionality, while monotonicity converts bounded tail ratios exactly into uniform block-geometric decay. Boundary n=1 and geometric/slow scales were evaluated. The included verifier completed 15 fully enumerated finite cases and 60 independent LP norm checks, supporting but not replacing the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The exact operator constants distinguish a natural canonical monotone Schauder basis from the abstract ell_1 isomorphism class. The uniform block-geometric threshold classifies precisely when this retractional basis is unconditional and supplies all finite-section sharp constants, rather than an isolated example or a small numerical improvement. The example of a uniformly discrete strictly decreasing comb with conditional nearest-point basis shows real geometric dependence of this natural approximation method. No downstream theorem is asserted.
